title: Sunny and the Moonbow | Bedtime Story
description: Sunny the Quokka sees something she has never seen before — a moonbow, a pale white rainbow made by moonlight through the mist, there and almost not there, the most magical thing in the bush. A gentle bedtime story for toddlers from Sunny's Little Bedtime Stories.
narration:
She almost didn't believe what she was seeing.

The mist had come up from the creek, rolling softly into the clearing, and the full moon was high and bright. And there, in the mist — low over the bush, barely visible — was a bow. A moonbow. A rainbow made not of sunlight but of moonlight, pale and white and almost not there at all.

She blinked.

It was still there.

Not the vivid colours of a rainbow — just white, with a faint ghost of colour if she looked at the edges very carefully. It curved from somewhere in the mist to somewhere in the dark beyond the trees, a soft pale arc.

She had never seen one before. She had heard that moonbows existed — that the moon could do what the sun did, but quietly, secretly, in the middle of the night when almost no one was watching.

Almost no one.

She sat down in the dewy grass.

The moonbow was too soft to stare at — it seemed to become less visible the more directly she looked at it. She had to look a little to the side, let it stay at the edge of her vision. And there it was. A pale, patient arc of light.

She thought: the most magical things are the quietest ones.

The mist shifted. The moonbow held for a moment longer, then gently dissolved.

She lay back in the grass.

Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, moonbow. Goodnight, little one.
